key_facts: Patient has complex congenital heart disease
Patient has D-transposition of the great arteries
Patient experiences lightheadedness and syncope with walking
Patient has persistent tachycardia and palpitations
ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating
Transesophageal echocardiogram shows no intracardiac thrombus
Patient is prescribed diltiazem and apixaban
Heart rate is 183 bpm in the emergency department

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG shows irregularly irregular tachycardia with grouped beating and intermittently visible P waves, which is consistent with intra-atrial reentrant tachycardia, especially in the context of Fontan circulation and complex congenital heart disease.

rejected.label: Orthodromic Atrioventricular Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: The ECG does not show a consistent pattern of retrograde P waves, which is typically seen in orthodromic atrioventricular reentrant tachycardia.

rejected.label: Atrioventricular Nodal Reentrant Tachycardia
rejected.why: The patient's response to adenosine, which typically terminates atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, only showed temporary heart block without terminating the tachycardia.
